main_text.p: pulsi, tamen in agro Euchrociæ aliquantisper morati, infecere nonnullos suis erroribus. Inde iter coeptum ingressi, turpi sane pudibundoq; comitatu, cum uxoribus atq; alienis etiam fœminis, in quis erat{a} Eu-chrocia, ac filia ejus Procula: de qua fuit in sermone hominum, Priscilliani stupro gravidamVide no. tas., partum sibi graminibus abegisse. Hi ubi Romam pervenere, Damaso le purgare cupientes, ne in conspectum quidem ejus admissi sunt. Regressi Mediolanum, æque aversantem sibi Ambrosiū repererunt. Tum vertere consilia, ut quia duobus episcopis, quorum ea tempestate summa authoritas erat, non illuserant, largiendo & ambiendo ab imperatore cupita extorquerent. ita corrupto Macedo-nio, tum forte.{b}cum magistro officiorum, referi-ptum eliciunt, quo calcaris quæ prius decreta erant, restitui ecclesiis jubebantur. Hoc freti Iustantius & Priscillianus, repetivere Hispanias. Nam Salvianus in urbe obierat: ac tum sine ullo certamine ecclesias, quibus præfuerant, recepere. Ve-rū{c} Trachio ad resistendum non animus, sed facultas defuit: quia hæretici corrupto Volventio proconsule, vires suas confir-maverant,Idacio.

page.notes: The left margin notes "a uxor" and "b tum forte." and "c Idacio." are placed at the lines where the reference marks stand; the "Vide no. tas." note is uncertain and may read differently. Marks a, b, c are small superscript letters in the text, reproduced as {a}, {b}, {c}. The marginal "e" before Idacio looks like "c" and may be "e". The small mark at the bottom left of the page and the stain at the lower right are not printed text and were left out. Hyphenated line-end words kept their printed hyphens (Eu-chrocia, Macedo-nio, referi-ptum, confir-maverant, Ve-rū).
